sentences.text: Coahomasuchus is an extinct genus belonging to the aetosaurine group of aetosaurs.
This animal was small for an aetosaur, measuring less than 1.5 meters in length.
Its dorsal plates were distinctively flat and unflexed with faint sub-parallel to radial ornamentation.
Unlike many other aetosaurs, Coahomasuchus lacked spines or keels on its dorsal plates.
The holotype of C. chathamensis includes parts of the skull, a feature that is rare among aetosaurs.
Sharp, recurved teeth indicate a carnivorous diet, a trait shared only with Aetosauroides among aetosaurs.
Fossils of Coahomasuchus have been discovered in Texas and North Carolina from Late Triassic deposits dating to the Otischalkian faunachron.
The type species C. kahleorum was named by Heckert and Lucas in 1999.
A second species, C. chathamensis, was named by Heckert et al. in 2017 from the Pekin Formation of the Newark Supergroup.
Coahomasuchus belongs to the parent group Aetosaurinae.
The genus is classified within the family Stagonolepididae.
Coahomasuchus is classified as a reptile.
Coahomasuchus lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
